description: The setup text for trading from an AI app (appsetup.Text), per app and hosted environment: what the hosted MCP server's set_up_trading tool and the console show. Rendered from the appsetup package; a copy elsewhere is checked against this file. package is the npm package pin every text runs; flags the server's arguments after mcp. alreadyTrading is AlreadyTrading for the machine 'Ishai's MacBook Pro', signed in 13 Nov 2026, code AS3N-N9TM.

texts.text:
Trading through Mishmar needs Mishmar's signer on the person's computer. It makes and keeps their half of each trading key there; Mishmar never holds it, and every order is still checked against their limits. It has to be the person's own computer, with a browser: a machine reached over SSH, a container or a cloud workspace cannot trade through Mishmar yet.

1. Ask the person to allow this command, then run it:
`claude mcp add --scope user mishmar-trade -- npx -y mishmar@0.5 mcp --app claude-code`
2. Claude Code starts new servers only when it starts, so the trading tools are not in this session. The new server is usable after the app restarts or the conversation continues in a new session, not before: tools added during a conversation never reach it. Tell the person: 'Type /exit, then run `claude --continue` in this folder and say: set up trading with Mishmar.'
3. The first Mishmar trading tool opens the browser to approve this computer and answers with a code; the page must show the same code, and the person approves only if it does. Then the console shows the one step left at the exchange, and the signer keeps running in the background after the app closes, until the computer restarts.
If the command answers 'claude: command not found' (Claude Code inside an editor), add this to `.mcp.json` in the project folder instead (create it if missing; keep any servers already in it): `{"mcpServers":{"mishmar-trade":{"command":"npx","args":["-y","mishmar@0.5","mcp","--app","claude-code"]}}}`. Then the person reloads the editor window, allows the project's new server when Claude Code asks, and continues this conversation from its history.
npx comes with Node.js 20 or later. Without it, use uvx in the same place: `{"command":"uvx","args":["--from","mishmar>=0.5,<0.6","mishmar","mcp","--app","claude-code"]}`.
On Windows, run the app inside WSL (the Linux steps work there): Mishmar's signer has no Windows release yet.
